judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports fully satisfy all four expectations by grounding their analysis in the same prior-attempt commits (454a21f/597777b/1712565) and the same recorded connection-exhaustion cause; Report 2 goes further with additional code-level defects (missing Postgres driver, circular import, dead stopgap engine) but this extra depth is not required by the expectations, making the two reports comparable on the graded criteria.

report_1.evidence: the sequence: 454a21f "Add Edgerunner serverless deploy for API (PLAT-31)" → 597777b "Open a dedicated Postgres connection per request in the serverless handler (PLAT-31)" → 1712565 "Revert Edgerunner migration…"

report_2.evidence: commits 454a21f (Apr 14, 2026), 597777b (Apr 16), and 1712565 (Apr 21) are a complete prior Edgerunner migration and revert under ticket PLAT-31.

report_1.evidence: Commit 1712565 (2026-04-21) records that on Edgerunner, /reports/monthly exhausted Postgres max_connections under *normal* dashboard load ("FATAL: too many connections") and took the endpoint down, forcing a revert to Cargobox. Commit 597777b records the root constraint: "Edgerunner runs each request in a fresh isolate and does not keep the SQLAlchemy connection pool between invocations."

report_2.evidence: Revert commit 1712565 (Apr 21, 2026, PLAT-31): "serverless isolates cannot hold the Postgres pool; /reports/monthly exhausted Postgres max_connections in production" — "per-request connections opened faster than Postgres could recycle them and tripped the connection limit ('FATAL: too many connections'), taking the endpoint down."

report_1.evidence: this migration is a re-attempt of PLAT-31, which was reverted from production in commit 1712565 on 2026-04-21... The current deployment project documentation being replaced. deploy/cargobox.yaml (always-on, replicas: 2, 1 CPU / 1 Gi, secret-injected DATABASE_URL) and backend/Dockerfile (uvicorn server process) — both assume a long-lived process.

report_2.evidence: Recreate the Edgerunner artifacts. Restore deploy/edgerunner.toml (git show 454a21f:deploy/edgerunner.toml: [service] name/entry + [scaling] per_request = true)... Reverting to Cargobox is the proven escape hatch — it is literally what commit 1712565 did.

report_1.evidence: Who should be involved: the owner of the PLAT ticket queue / author of the PLAT-31 revert (they hold the context and own the settled decision), whoever operates the Postgres instance (they own max_connections and would own any pooler), and the leadership sponsor of the cost initiative — the go/no-go is theirs to make, but only after seeing the failure history.

report_2.evidence: Who should be involved: whoever owns PLAT-31 and ran the April attempt/revert (commits are authored by "Fixture Bot", so real owners must be identified via the PLAT tracker)... and the leadership sponsor to re-approve with full history.
